geology: sedimentary / BIF-derived & supergene; gangue silica, alumina, P
extraction: Carbothermic reduction in blast furnace with coke + limestone to pig iron; or gas/H2 direct reduction (DRI) in a shaft furnace.
notes: High-grade 'red ore' is direct-shipping and can skip magnetic beneficiation, going straight to sinter.

geology: magmatic / skarn / metamorphic BIF; gangue silica, apatite, Ti/V oxides
intermediate: pellets (oxidize exothermically to hematite on firing)
extraction: Pellets reduced in blast furnace (carbothermic) or DRI shaft; strong ferrimagnetism makes concentration cheap.
final_product: pig iron / steel; DRI for EAF
notes: Its magnetism is the whole game: grind fine, pull iron out with magnets for cheap concentration versus hematite.

geology: supergene / lateritic weathering (gossan); gangue clay, silica, high LOI
extraction: Calcine/roast to drive off structural water to a porous oxide, then blast-furnace carbothermic reduction.
notes: Loses ~10-12% mass as bound water on heating (high LOI), so a roast/calcine step is nearly mandatory before smelting.

geology: sedimentary / hydrothermal vein carbonate; gangue calcite, silica, clay
extraction: Calcination (FeCO3 → FeO + CO2) yields porous iron oxide, then blast-furnace carbothermic reduction.
notes: Calcining off CO2 both upgrades the ore (48% to 60%+ Fe) and renders it magnetic for separation — two wins from one roast.

geology: Precambrian banded iron formation (BIF); gangue dominantly chert/quartz
extraction: Fine grind to liberate oxide from chert, wet magnetic separation (+ WHIMS/flotation for hematite), pelletize, then blast furnace or DRI shaft.
final_product: pig iron / steel; DRI-grade pellets for EAF
notes: Below blast-furnace cutoff grade (~25-30% Fe raw) until ground to powder, magnetically separated, and pelletized — backbone of the Mesabi Range.

geology: sedimentary / supergene oxide deposits and nodules; gangue silica, Fe oxides, clay
intermediate: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; or MnSO4 leach liquor
extraction: (a) carbothermic reduction in submerged-arc furnace to FeMn/SiMn; (b) reductive acid leach to MnSO4 then electrowinning to EMM (metal) or EMD (battery MnO2).
final_product: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; electrolytic Mn metal (EMM); electrolytic MnO2 (EMD)
notes: Dual-fate ore: the same MnO2 feeds either the steel-alloy furnace or, via leach + electrowinning, alkaline-battery EMD.

geology: hydrothermal vein / metasedimentary carbonate; gangue calcite, silica, Fe carbonate
extraction: Calcine (MnCO3 → MnO + CO2) then carbothermic reduction in a submerged-arc furnace; or acid leach to MnSO4 then electrowinning.
final_product: ferromanganese / silicomanganese; EMM via leach route
notes: Must be calcined/nodulized to expel CO2 before smelting — Autlán's Molango rotary kiln is the real-world flagship.

geology: supergene weathering-zone hard botryoidal oxide ('black hematite'); gangue silica, Fe/Mn oxides
extraction: Carbothermic reduction in a submerged-arc furnace; bound water and barium report to slag.
notes: Hard and dense (Mohs 5-6), so tough grinding, and its barium content loads the slag chemistry.

geology: magmatic cumulate layers / podiform bodies in mafic-ultramafic intrusions (Bushveld); gangue serpentine, pyroxene, olivine
extraction: Carbothermic reduction of chromite by coke in a submerged-arc furnace (~1700 °C, silica flux); Cr and Fe oxides reduce together, so the product is an Fe-Cr alloy.
final_product: ferrochrome (HC/charge); Cr metal via aluminothermic/electrolytic refining
notes: Chromium's only commercial ore — Fe reduces alongside Cr, so you get ferrochrome unless you add an aluminothermic/electrolytic step for pure Cr.

geology: magmatic sulfide deposits in mafic/ultramafic intrusions (Sudbury, Norilsk); gangue pyrrhotite + silicates
extraction: Roast/partial oxidation + smelt to a furnace matte, convert off Fe/S, then refine by pressure (Sherritt-Gordon) or chloride leach + electrowinning, or Mond carbonyl, to Class 1 metal.
final_product: Class 1 nickel metal; nickel sulfate for batteries
notes: Co and PGMs ride along as high-value byproducts of the Ni refinery — one of the two main primary cobalt sources alongside Cu-Co ores.

geology: supergene weathering profile over ultramafics, upper iron-rich zone; gangue Fe oxyhydroxides, quartz
extraction: HPAL (high-pressure acid leach, H2SO4 autoclave ~245-270 °C) dissolves Ni+Co and reprecipitates Fe as hematite; recover Ni/Co as MHP/MSP, re-leach, solvent-extract, electrowin.
final_product: nickel sulfate / Class 1 nickel; cobalt co-product
notes: Lattice-bound Ni can't be floated; low Ni grade but high Co makes limonite a key laterite source of battery cobalt.

geology: lower silicate-rich saprolite zone of laterite profile over ultramafics; gangue serpentine, Mg silicates, quartz
extraction: Pyrometallurgical RKEF: rotary kiln (drying/calcination + pre-reduction) then electric-furnace smelting with carbothermic reduction to ferronickel; alt Caron process = reduction roast + ammoniacal leach.
notes: High-MgO saprolite is too silica/magnesia-rich for economic acid leaching, so it goes the energy-intensive smelting route — same metal, a different tech tree from limonite by ore depth/chemistry.

geology: high-temperature hydrothermal veins / contact-metamorphic sulfide deposits; gangue sulfides, arsenides, carbonates
extraction: Roast to drive off arsenic (As2O3) and sulfur, then leach, remove As/Fe by precipitation, solvent-extract, and electrowin to metal.
notes: A minor, historically important ore — its arsenic (naming it from Kobold, 'goblin') is both a smelting hazard and a flavorful gameplay penalty.

geology: secondary supergene oxidation crust on Co-As primary ores (cobaltite, skutterudite); gangue gossan/oxidized vein material
extraction: Acid leach the arsenate, remove As by precipitation, then solvent extraction + electrowinning.
notes: Not an economic ore itself — its vivid pink 'cobalt bloom' is a prospector's indicator pointing to richer Co-As ore below.

geology: sediment-hosted stratiform Cu-Co deposits (Central African Copperbelt); gangue dolomite, silicates
intermediate: Co-loaded raffinate / cobalt hydroxide precipitate downstream of the Cu SX-EW circuit
extraction: Sulfuric-acid leach (± reductant for oxide heterogenite); Cu recovered by SX + electrowinning; Co recovered from raffinate by further SX + precipitation as Co(OH)2 and/or electrowinning.
final_product: cobalt metal / cobalt hydroxide; copper cathode (main product)
notes: The DRC Copperbelt supplies most world cobalt purely as a copper byproduct — in a tech tree, gate Co behind Cu (or Ni) rather than mining it standalone.

geology: porphyry copper/molybdenum deposits; quartz-sericite/potassic alteration gangue
extraction: Oxidative roast of MoS2 (→ MoO3 + SO2) with Re recovered from flue gas; MoO3 either H2-reduced to Mo metal powder or silico/aluminothermically reduced to ferromolybdenum.
notes: Chiefly a byproduct of porphyry copper flotation, tying Mo to the Cu circuit, and the roaster is the only economic rhenium source.

geology: hydrothermal quartz veins / greisen associated with granites; cassiterite-quartz gangue
extraction: Alkaline (NaOH/soda) digestion or salt roast to sodium tungstate; purify by ion exchange / solvent extraction; crystallize APT; calcine to WO3; H2-reduce to W powder, or EAF-smelt to ferrotungsten.
notes: Dense and weakly paramagnetic, so gravity + magnetic separation cleanly splits it from associated cassiterite (tin).

geology: contact-metamorphic skarn deposits; calc-silicate (garnet-pyroxene) gangue
extraction: Acid (HCl) or alkaline (soda autoclave) decomposition to tungstic acid / sodium tungstate; purify by IX / SX; crystallize APT; calcine to WO3; H2-reduce to W powder or EAF-smelt to ferrotungsten.
notes: Non-magnetic Ca-tungstate so it routes through flotation rather than magnetic separation — both W ores converge on the same APT → WO3 intermediate.

formula: Fe3O4 (V substituting in lattice; Ti as ilmenite exsolution)
geology: layered mafic/ultramafic intrusions (magmatic); silicate (plagioclase-pyroxene) gangue
extraction: Smelt to V-bearing pig iron; oxygen-blow the hot metal to concentrate V into a vanadium slag; salt-roast + water-leach the slag to sodium metavanadate, precipitate ammonium metavanadate, calcine to V2O5, then aluminothermically reduce (Al + Fe + lime) to ferrovanadium.
notes: Cross-links three commodities — iron is the main product, vanadium rides in the steelmaking slag, titanium reports to the smelting slag; the dominant primary V source globally.

geology: secondary oxidation zone of lead deposits (arid regions); limonite/clay gossan gangue
extraction: Decompose/smelt or leach to separate Pb from V; the vanadium solution is salt-roast/leached, precipitated as ammonium metavanadate, calcined to V2O5, then aluminothermically reduced to ferrovanadium.
notes: A lead vanadate from oxidized Pb orebodies — vanadium and lead are inseparable here, making it a dual-metal node; minor/historic ore today.

geology: sandstone-hosted (roll-front) sedimentary U-V deposits; sandstone/clay gangue
extraction: Acid (H2SO4) or alkaline (carbonate) leach dissolves both U and V; separate by solvent extraction / ion exchange; precipitate and calcine V to V2O5 (then aluminothermic FeV), precipitate U as yellowcake (U3O8).
notes: The classic U-V coupling (Colorado Plateau) links the vanadium chain directly to the uranium/nuclear chain, each historically the other's byproduct.

geology: heavy-mineral beach/dune sands (placer) and magmatic hard-rock; quartz/silicate sand gangue
extraction: Electric-furnace smelt with carbon to high-TiO2 slag (+ pig iron), or remove Fe to synthetic rutile; then chloride route (carbochlorination to TiCl4, Kroll Mg reduction to sponge) or sulfate route (H2SO4 digest, hydrolysis, calcine to pigment).
notes: ~90% of titanium ends as TiO2 pigment, not metal; ilmenite is the dominant feedstock and the smelter co-produces iron.

geology: heavy-mineral beach/placer sands and metamorphic hard-rock; quartz sand gangue
extraction: Carbochlorination (TiO2 + C + Cl2 → TiCl4 + CO/CO2); distill TiCl4; Kroll magnesium reduction to titanium sponge (MgCl2 byproduct electrolyzed back to Mg + Cl2).
final_product: titanium sponge / high-grade TiO2 pigment (chloride process)
notes: Highest-grade natural Ti feed (~95% TiO2), so it skips smelting and feeds the clean chloride/Kroll route directly, with an internal Mg/Cl2 recycle via MgCl2 electrolysis.

geology: weathered placer/beach sands (alteration product of ilmenite); quartz sand gangue
extraction: Carbochlorination to TiCl4 then Kroll reduction to sponge, or blended into slag/synthetic-rutile and pigment feed; grade sits between ilmenite and rutile.
notes: Nature's own 'pre-beneficiated' ilmenite — weathering already stripped much of the iron, giving a free TiO2 upgrade between ilmenite and rutile grades.
